reader.requirement: At --std 85, when all key data items of two or more records compare equal under the relation-condition rules (including the MERGE's COLLATING SEQUENCE, so ALSO-equated characters tie), the merged records must come back in the order of the USING files as written in the MERGE statement, all of one file's tied records before any of the next file's, for every organization of USING file, for the GIVING and the OUTPUT PROCEDURE forms, in memory or spilled to disk.
reader.edition-search: Grepped CobolSort.cs, SortWork.cs and SortEmitter.cs for Edition|DialectLevel|CobolVersion|Std: no match. SortBinder.BindMerge consults the edition only through ctx.Edition as a diagnostic sink and in ScreenSameClauses (held1985, SAME RECORD AREA, SORT only) - nothing on the tie order. The emitter calls SortNextInput once per USING file in statement order and the runtime's one merge cursor (strict less-than, earliest run wins) is edition-blind, so 85 and 2023 run the same code.

reader.notes: Each USING file is its own stream (NextStream at each file's start); the in-memory slices and the on-disk runs are merged by the one SortMergeCursor whose strict less-than lets an equal head never displace an earlier stream, and consolidation merges only consecutive streams, so GR4a and GR4b hold in both regimes. No edition arm exists or is needed.

MERGE USING F1 F2 printed -1F1-1 -0F1-2 +0F1-3 +0F2-1 -0F2-2 +1F2-3, and USING F2 F1 printed -1F1-1 +0F2-1 -0F2-2 -0F1-2 +0F1-3 +1F2-3. Both match: the compare is algebraic, not bytewise.
